evidence: task/instruction.md (5 lines, 683 bytes, three prose paragraphs) reads cold as a person asking for a tool. Line 1: "I'd like a small local playground for working on JavaScript and complete HTML files. The editor itself matters: I often paste a long one-line experiment, format it, make changes in several places, and then run it beside the source. I want to keep the versions that work without losing a draft when another tab saves first." Line 3 points to the notes ("Please read the six notes in /instructions before building"; six files exist) and line 5 states only the delivery location and outcome ("Put the app in /app and serve the workspace at /. I should be able to open it, edit code, run it and inspect the result without signing in."). Checked against the defect list in references/quality-checks.md check 1: a grep for list markers and table pipes (^[-*] , ^N. , |) over instruction.md and all six notes returns nothing, so there is no numbered acceptance list, spec table or feature matrix; instruction.md contains zero 'must'/'shall'; and it names no framework, file layout or endpoint list (grep for react|vite|typescript|express|sqlite|/api/ in instruction.md returns nothing). The runtime facts that could look like a recipe (node /app/server.js, 0.0.0.0:3000, GET /api/health, SQLite, DB_PATH) live in environment/instructions/integration.md and mirror the frozen template's own integration.md, which check 4 requires to be stated; integration.md line 5 and policy.md line 3 explicitly leave routes, frontend tools, layout, labels and schema to the builder ("You may choose your routes and frontend tools"), so no build recipe is imposed. Observation that does not change the verdict: the notes are requirement-dense prose rather than a casual ask. ui.md is 900 words in 8 paragraphs and behaviour.md carries 10 'must' in 514 words (21 'must' across the six notes), e.g. behaviour.md line 7 "Timers, intervals and Promise callbacks still pending from a stopped run must never change the preview or the console afterwards." They stay in paragraphs with first-person framing (ui.md line 9 "for as long as I keep typing at those carets, however slowly"; behaviour.md line 11 "That refresh must not touch what I'm doing"), which is the house structure of a short ask plus detailed notes, and the workbook row and skill procedure are scoped to instruction.md (block 'A - instruction.md', 'read instruction.md cold'). The density is the result of several QC rounds tightening wording; further additions in that style would push ui.md and behaviour.md toward a spec sheet in paragraph form. No runtime evidence is needed for this row.
